cohort: The cohort consisted of 605 patients diagnosed with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) between 2014 and 2021, identified from a single institution's research database.
finding: Nearly 60% of patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC) had at least one prior abdominal or pelvic surgery, indicating a missed opportunity for risk reduction through opportunistic salpingectomy decades before diagnosis.
followup_time: median 30.0 years (IQR 19.4-37.7) between first index surgery and HGSOC diagnosis
